title: MCV (Mean Corpuscular Volume)
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Measures the average size of the red blood cells. An unusual size may point to a blood disorder such as anemia, a vitamin deficiency or another condition.
low: Smaller-than-usual cells are associated with iron deficiency anemia, the most common form of anemia, and with thalassemia, a group of inherited blood disorders.
high: Larger-than-usual cells are associated with pernicious anemia (which may follow a lack of vitamin B12 or a condition affecting how it is used, such as certain autoimmune diseases, celiac disease or Crohn's disease), anemia from a lack of folic acid, and liver disease.
notes: Anemia can also occur with a normal MCV, for example after sudden blood loss or with kidney failure. The test alone cannot diagnose a disease, and age, diet, activity, medicines and periods can affect it.
